This is actually a false dichotomy which was formed by mistakenly understanding where the real "fork of logic" in the story is found.

Your fork is something like this: The first answer assumes humanity had no alternate means of a good life in the absence of the "fruit of the knowledge of good and evil." The second assumes that the "fruit of the knowledge of good and evil" was something necessarily good in itself. The first answer doubts God's good intentions. The second assumes that Adam and Eve had an issue that needed to be corrected.

The actual dichotomy we're meant to draw is between the "fruit of the knowledge of good and evil" and "the fruit of the tree of life." Both options in the garden are provided by God. The fruit of life works by trusting God and relying on Him. He knows our needs and provides for them. He allows us to choose what we do, but we are also imperfect creatures capable of error. The "fruit of the knowledge of good and evil" is about exploitation of the principle of good and evil to serve our own desires. It's not merely knowledge in itself. One of the capacities it can generate is obviously not evil: Knowing good and evil and choosing to avoid evil. But this is inherently negative and contrary to our initial vector of energy. The natural vector of energy is positive and causes the default choice to be misdirected towards choosing evil because of the influence of this "fruit."

This flaw that created Original Sin is that our natural course, which worked fine without this knowledge, was not yet ready to handle this knowledge properly. Our state of sin is the composition of the inherent imperfections of humanity being coupled with an idolization of the consequences of pursuing imperfect desires without regards for the universal truth of God. Had we been properly reoriented toward a negative capacity, this issue would have taken a different form and we would not have had the Fall because our default state would remain "not doing evil" while keeping the principle of "trusting God."

God's role is operating as the stand-in of reality itself. The net consequence of having the convergence be inverted by knowledge being misapplied as a natural disposition is that humanity became oriented towards both pointless shame and self-serving arrogance. The pointless shame leads us to desperation which leads us to do more arrogant acts to fulfill our incorrectly perceived "works quota." God isn't a taskmaster. He's a Father. But our ego wrongly makes Him out as a taskmaster because of our shame.

Theologians describe the consequences as "curving inward into oneself." The desires of humanity have become "inflamed" to make our own whims the most important thing. Our desires have replaced the definition of "good and evil." Instead of truth, they are now defined by futile pursuit of flawed desires without regard to actual consequences.

What did the serpent suggest? "Ye shall be as God." Yet God had created Adam and Eve in His image already. The flaw is apparent. Eve did not realize she already had everything good and desired something else instead. What was Eve's response? Despair and doubt. You can see her response in adding to what God said. She didn't say God merely limited them not to eating the fruit, as the text stated, but she also added "do not touch." This is indicative of the lack of trust and absolute untruthfulness of her desire The desire for knowledge became inflamed and warped into a self-serving goal. Thus, she not only defied the warning, but also dragged someone else in to defy it with her.

Our moral is a warning against abuse. Do not forget that something good in a proper context can be harmful outside of it. Knowledge is good when it is kept in its proper context. However, its fruits do not really belong to us. The ultimate arbiter of truth is God. Willfully rejecting the truth for our own desires has harmful consequences. But desires are good when used to pursue healthy goals. Do not succumb to the lure of pursuing imperfect desires to the point of futility. Do not make the perfect the enemy of the good. We must be humble enough to know that our understanding is incomplete.

The real "binding" principle of Original Sin is that our inherent decisions are predisposed to include some error. We must compensate for the error by allowing God to be God and not arrogantly assuming we have no capacity for mistakes.

God KNOWS He made us with the capacity for mistakes. God's response was not just causing Adam and Eve to just die of the consequences as the Law alone would warrant but coupled this with a promise of mercy to those who rely on Him. A physical death would eventually come, but a final resurrection was promised where death itself would be put to flight. A spiritual death was met with a process of reconciliation which involved "changing one's mind" and learning to trust God again through His mercy which puts to death the arrogant ego and restores a person to communion with God through the work of His Living Word.
